name: wf-postmortem
description: wf postmortem pack: the postmortem capability, a presence-only feature that ships a guided skill hunting a described failure through prior agent sessions in scope — named explicitly with --session, or located automatically under a resolved scope behind one replaceable seam that owns all host-specific knowledge of the session store, its layout, and the 30-day retention window, and fails loudly on an unrecognized record shape. Every located session is ranked (scope-match specificity, then recency, hunt sessions always last) without ever being silently dropped, and read up to a per-run cap (default 15, overridable with --cap) — every session beyond it is listed skipped (budget), retrievable by a later --report <path> follow-up that reads those sessions and extends the same report file in place. Each session is read by its own isolated reader agent on a cheaper model tier — in ordered windows when a record is too large for one reader — so raw session content never enters the host context; a located session's iterations, edits, and files-touched counts are mechanically observed wherever the seam counts them deterministically. Every reader-suggested mechanism with a locator is then checked two-sided, against the audited pack's own text at its resolved executed version and against a bounded, redacted excerpt fetched fresh at the locator, and promoted to a confirmed contributing factor only when both sides verify. The report then states a fix direction, apart from the evidence, marked stated or resting on an open choice, and closes with a rule-based recommendation naming the next workflow — dispatching and filing nothing itself. Owns no provider surface and attaches no phase fragment — it ships inert until registered and behaves identically whether or not it is. Fallback evidence from task folders and delivery history arrives with a later charter sub-task. Ships /wf-postmortem:postmortem, the guided skill, plus /wf-postmortem:init for one-command self-registration.
